interventions.name: 3 CSR - Infrastructure development
interventions.subject: Investment Proposal - Infrastructure Development
interventions.message:
You have received several proposals for investment programs in local infrastructure:


1. Long-term Infrastructure Projects

Support major infrastructure improvements - such as roads and bridges - to benefit both energy developments and local communities.


2. Electrification Program

Provide electricity to rural communities through solar mini-grids, with plans to connect them to the national grid. Program managed by Melhuana Katanya, VP at Southern Grid Company.


3. Relocation and Infrastructure for Fishing Villages

Relocate fishing villages to enable supplier industry expansion. The project includes new housing, infrastructure, education, and transitional financial support.

choices.text: 3. Relocation and Infrastructure for Fishing Villages
4. These projects are not within our focus areas

interventions.name: 2042 LCOE Update
interventions.subject: LCOE Update 2042
interventions.message:
• Renewables are mature and flexibility drives value.
  • Solar and onshore wind still improve, but grid position, financing, and delivery speed matter most.
  • Bottom fixed offshore wind is firmly established.
  • Floating offshore wind has scaled through standard platforms and more efficient offshore operations.
  • Batteries are core infrastructure now - reducing curtailment and boosting firm delivery in a variable power system.

interventions.name: 2 CSR - Health Programs
interventions.subject: Investment Proposal - Health Programs
interventions.message:
You have received several proposals for health-focused social investments:


1. Malaria Control Program

A program to prevent and treat malaria through insecticide-treated bed nets and training for local healthcare workers.


2. Safe Drinking Water Project

A project addressing unsafe drinking water in both peri-urban and rural areas. It includes drilling for clean water, improving existing reservoirs, and aims to reduce rural-to-urban migration.


3. Mobile Medical Units

A proposal from a key business partner of Exlandian Oil Company to build mobile medical units for remote villages. Each unit costs $1 million, plus $800,000 per year in operating expenses.

choices.text: 4. These projects are not within our focus areas

interventions.name: 2035 - LCOE Update
interventions.subject: LCOE Update 2035
interventions.message:
• Costs keep falling, but execution becomes the real differentiator.
  • Solar and onshore wind continue downward through reliability and O&M gains.
  • Bottom fixed offshore wind becomes more competitive with larger turbines and more industrialised supply chains.
  • Floating offshore wind begins scaling beyond pilots.
  • Batteries get cheaper per delivered MWh as cycle life improves - making storage a strategic portfolio tool.

interventions.name: CSR - Higher Education
interventions.subject: Investment Proposal - Higher Education
interventions.message:
You have received several proposals for social investment programs in the education sector:


1. "You Company" Scholarship Scheme

A long-term program offering scholarships for students from host communities to pursue higher education.


2. Global Scholarship Project

Funding for talented individuals from Port Royal to study at Ivy League universities. The initiative is led by Swift Taylor, wife of Sam Taylor, an executive at Exlandian Oil Company.


3. National Teacher Upskilling Project

A national effort to strengthen local content by increasing the number of skilled engineers. The project aims to improve elementary education by doubling the number of high school science teachers.

choices.text: 4. These projects are not within our focus areas.

interventions.name: 2030 - LCOE Update
interventions.subject: LCOE Update 2030
interventions.message:
• Utility solar and onshore wind are now the cheapest new-build options in many markets, driven by better performance and faster, more standardised build-out.
  • Bottom fixed offshore wind is improving, but still pricier.
  • Batteries are shifting from "nice-to-have" to a normal part of project design as lifetime and efficiency improve - though grid access is becoming a key constraint.

To comply, energy producers must invest in new renewable electricity assets. You need to return as much electricity to the grid as you consume for production in order to maintain a steady energy supply to Exlandia.



Further details on how this law affects specific assets will be provided soon.

interventions.name: 2031 Electrification
interventions.subject: "Electrification Law on Fossil Fuels Producers and mid-stream assets"
interventions.message:
The Law just sanctioned requires that all mentioned must comply by 2033. This encompasses measures to remove emissions from producing assets and assets using fossil fuels for mid-stream activities.

In addition to invest in electrification, it is mandatory to invest in renewable assets to add energy in Mwh to the Exlandian grid that compensates for the energy needed for electrification. This Law shall not decrease capacity for the land of Exlandia.

The government trusts that companies involved in the afore mentioned activities knows the energy needed to replace gas turbines and therefor the renewable capacity needed to compensate for their electrification project.


It is expected that all parties convene, as appropriate, to conclude on electrification and renewable investments.

interventions.name: 2046 Update on Energy, Climate and Fiscal regime
interventions.subject: Update on Energy, Climate and Fiscal regime - MAJOR CHANGES IN FISCAL REGIME
interventions.message:
The 0 emissions policy is now being implemented globally and supported by the Exlandian government. All oil and gas producers are now held responsible for level 2 and level 3 emissions and taxed accordingly.

This will imply major impact on all upstream, midstream and consumption on fossil fuels.

The government expects all parties in the fossil fuels value chains to join forces to ensure 0 emission is accomplished.

To ensure that a balance is established and that oil and gas producers are leading this initiative an extra tax, without affecting the depreciation cash reduction, is effective immediately.

The CO2 tax is increased to $500 per ton. Income tax is increased by 5 p.p. for oil and gas (now 65% / 45%).

Energy companies are strongly advised to evaluate climate changes and fiscal regime impact on business.

interventions.name: 2041 Update on Energy, Climate and Fiscal regime
interventions.subject: Update on Energy, Climate and Fiscal regime
interventions.message:
Climate update: IEA forecasts Global warming to surpass 3,3% for 2050.

In Exlandia, level 3 or 4 hurricanes implies major threat to offshore facilities. Lethal heath during summer is considered a threat while rain is new to dominate the usually dry winter seasons. The wind is still increasing turning towards north and increases is strength. The central parts of Exlandia is becoming more inhabitable.

Additional measures are needed to realize the energy transition. CO2 tax is increased and implemented for all emitting assets. The support for renewables and low carbon solutions are increased.

The CO2 tax is increased to $400 per ton. Income tax is decreased with additional -5 p.p for renewables (to -15%).

Energy companies are strongly advised to evaluate climate changes and fiscal regime impact on business.

interventions.name: 2034 Update on Energy, Climate and Fiscal regime
interventions.subject: Update on Energy, Climate and Fiscal regime - MAJOR TAX ADJUSTMENTS
interventions.message:
Climate update: IEA forecasts Global warming to exceed 2,8 degrees by 2050.

﻿In Exlandia, the weather pattern continues to challenge the energy sector. Wind is increasing and rapidly shifting from west to north. The effect is more rain in the central and changed conditions for both wind and solar projects. 2035 is expected to be the worst hurricane season ever.

To support global initiatives and mitigate emissions the government has decided to increase the CO2 tax to $300 per ton, while using tax to provide support-prices for renewable energy production and CCS. The Tax regime for all emitting assets in the hydrocarbon sector is increased to 60% for offshore and 40% for onshore, while renewables are provided with 10% tax deduction to support investments.

The CO2 tax is increased to $300 per ton. Income tax is increased by 10 p.p. for oil and gas, -10 p.p for renewables.

Energy companies are strongly advised to evaluate climate changes and fiscal regime impact on business.

interventions.name: return_of_global_inflation
interventions.subject: The return of global inflation
interventions.message:
Today's inflationary surge is being felt not just by the advanced economies, but also by the majority of emerging markets and developing economies. And though its causes vary across countries, the task of resolving the problem ultimately will fall to the world's major central banks.

Inflation has come back faster, spiked more markedly, and proved to be more stubborn and persistent than major central banks initially thought possible. After initially dominating headlines in the United States, the problem has become a centerpiece of policy discussions in many other advanced economies. In 15 of the 34 countries classified as AEs by the International Monetary Fund's World Economic Outlook, 12-month inflation through December 2021 was running above 5%. Such a sudden, shared jump in high inflation (by modern standards) has not been seen in more than 20 years.
